record.tranche_reason: The post reports results about how L0 affects feature mixing in a correlated toy model, but it does not test feature splitting as dictionary size increases or the other behaviors specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The post compares reconstruction and latent-feature geometry at different L0 values, with dictionary size fixed at 50. It does not vary dictionary size or report whether coarse feature inputs are partitioned among finer features.
record.test_reason: The post varies L0 (sparsity) with dictionary size fixed at 50 in a correlated toy model and reports feature mixing (hedging). It does not vary dictionary size, measure coarse-to-fine splitting, parent/child absorption, or cross-size decomposition. The finding is about the sparsity objective producing polysemantic latents, which relates to V6 in spirit but does not measure splitting, so it fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also state that L0 set too high fails to recover the true features. They add that their only reliable way to find the correct L0 is to train SAEs across a range of L0 values.
record.recipe_differences: Uses BatchTopK SAEs on a synthetic correlated-feature toy model and varies L0 while keeping dictionary size at 50; it does not vary dictionary size to test splitting.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature alignment changes between L0=1 and L0=11.

fits_no_version.finding: In a toy model with 50 correlated orthogonal features, BatchTopK SAEs with 50 latents trained at L0=1 learn polysemantic latents unrelated to the true features. The same SAEs recover the true features exactly at the true L0=11. The polysemantic SAE still reconstructs better than the ground-truth SAE at low L0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained with L0 below the true L0 mix correlated features (feature hedging) and gain reconstruction while losing monosemanticity. Sparsity-versus-reconstruction curves can therefore favour incorrect SAEs.

record.problems: The reported feature-alignment results come from one synthetic toy model; the post gives qualitative descriptions rather than numerical cosine values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: The post also shows sparsity-versus-reconstruction plots, but reports no numeric values in the text and those results do not measure feature splitting or input partitioning.

untested.parts: All parts: dictionary size is fixed at 50.
All parts: only a synthetic toy model is used.
All parts: no hierarchical features or feature families.
All parts: no parent/child latents. The L0 variation concerns correlated features, not absorption.
All parts: no comparison across SAE sizes.
Splitting and Matryoshka SAEs are not measured. The post shows the sparsity objective distorts latents (hedging) but not splitting.

record.verdict_notes: This is a blog companion to arXiv:2508.16560 ('Sparse but Wrong'). Results are qualitative descriptions of cosine-similarity plots, with no numbers given. The post's claim that too-high L0 also fails is stated but not shown in this text.

versions.untested_parts: Whether increasing dictionary size replaces a coarse feature with finer features that cover its inputs and lie near its direction.
Large models and open SAE releases; the post uses a toy model.
Nested, geometrically close feature families mirroring a hierarchy of concepts.
Parent-child firing overlap and whether size or sparsity changes fix absorption.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, novel latents, and whether any dictionary is a complete atomic set.
Feature splitting, Matryoshka SAEs, and whether the effect says anything about a model's own units. The post studies feature mixing under different L0 settings, not splitting.
